name: Game switch: year roll
when: The footage changes game: the cut from GTA VI footage to another game's footage (San Andreas, GTA IV, Red Dead 2), and the cut back to GTA VI after it (owner, 17 Nov 2026: never a direct cut between two games). One in and one out per run of another game's shots, the same variant both ways (series). The incoming game's logo (on the way back: the GTA VI logo) comes from assets/logos/ through `game`; a logo is never drawn or invented. The year roll says how far back (or forward) the video jumps: 2026 rolls back to the other game's year under its logo. Best when the year itself matters (a then-and-now comparison).
anchor: Mount it over the project's own hard cut between the two games' shots: start the scene `cut` (0.4 s) before the cut. The year rolls right after the cut, the logo lands, and the plate opens at `out`; the scene ends 0.33 s later on the new footage.
placement: Keep the project's footage as a plain hard cut. Mount the scene above both with make_scene --start <cut - 0.4>. The incoming shot plays under the plate and shows as the halves open.

vars.theme: clean (deep coral plate, white year) or vice (sunset plate, ink year): the video's theme
vars.game: the incoming game, as logos.json names it (going back: Grand Theft Auto VI)
vars.logo: its logo file: filled from assets/logos/ by build_video.mjs when `game` is listed there
vars.from: the outgoing game's year (2026 for GTA VI)
vars.year: the incoming game's year (2004 for San Andreas; 2026 on the way back)
vars.cut: seconds after the start: the hard cut under the plate (0.4)
vars.out: seconds after the start: when the plate opens (1.6)

lab: Not validated yet (built 17 Nov 2026 for the owner's note: 'when we clearly change game, a small clean transition in, and another one to come back to GTA 6'). Not in catalogue.md until he picks A, B or C.
